quotes.text: A Graph connector is a piece of software that brings external data into the Microsoft Graph. Now, the Microsoft Graph is the same index that powers Microsoft Search, SharePoint Search, and now Copilot.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Clear definition of what a Graph connector does and why it matters for Copilot.

quotes.text: With a federated connector, no data gets stored in Microsoft 365 at all. When a user asks co-pilot a question, co-pilot sends a request to the external system using the model context protocol or MCP.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains the federated connector model and its use of MCP.

quotes.text: you don't have to pick just one. Many organizations use both. They use synced connectors for their static knowledge base, HR policies, onboarding docs, reference materials, and they use federated connectors for their dynamic operational data.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Practical recommendation to combine both connector models.

quotes.text: Every single item that goes through a connector needs an access control list attached to it. That's an ACL. It tells Microsoft 365 who can see that piece of data.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Highlights the key security requirement when configuring connectors.

quotes.text: Co-pilot becomes truly useful when it can see all your company data. Not just what's sitting in SharePoint in one drive.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Summarizes the business case for connectors in one sentence.

chapters.title: Intro: Copilot's blind spot outside Microsoft 365
The problem: your data is everywhere

takeaways: Out of the box, Microsoft 365 Copilot only sees Microsoft 365 content; Graph connectors, now called Copilot connectors, bring external systems such as Salesforce, ServiceNow or Confluence into reach.
Synced connectors copy and semantically index data into Microsoft Graph, while federated connectors query the source live through the Model Context Protocol and store nothing in Microsoft 365.
Every connected item needs a correct access control list, and many organizations combine synced connectors for static knowledge with federated connectors for live operational data.
hook: Copilot cannot answer questions about data that lives in your CRM, ticketing system or wiki unless you connect it. This episode helps Microsoft 365 admins and Copilot owners understand Graph and Copilot connectors, choose between synced and federated models, and keep permissions and compliance intact.
